title: Case study: ticket booking
summary: Contended inventory: requirements and on-sale estimation, API and data model, oversell prevention (conditional writes, locks, constraints, isolation levels), holds with lazy expiry, general-admission counters, payment in flight with idempotent confirmation and reconciliation, and a flash-sale waiting room with signed passes.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design
Deep dives: oversell prevention and holds; payment in flight; the flash sale and the waiting room

labs.title: Virtual waiting room: idempotent FIFO joins with position and ETA, token-bucket admission capped at a burst, HMAC-signed passes with a TTL verified without a database, expiry, a bounded queue

outcomes.text: Scope a ticket-booking system in six minutes: the clarifying questions whose answers change the design (assigned seats vs general admission, the on-sale peak, holds and their TTL, how payment confirms, per-customer limits, fairness, other sellers) and the two hard invariants.

Estimate an on-sale (arrivals, demand ratio, seat-map reads and bandwidth, an admission rate from Little's law, queue wait and sell-out time, hold transactions per second, the single-row ceiling, storage) and tie each number to a decision.

Design the API (idempotent hold returning 409 with the seat, checkout that extends the hold once, signed webhook, server-side price) and a data model partitioned by event with seat rows, self-routing hold ids, limit rows and the unique constraints that make oversell and double processing impossible.
Draw the high-level design with the on-sale path through the waiting room, the booking path and the payment path traced, and justify every box by a requirement or a number.

Choose an oversell-prevention mechanism (conditional UPDATE, sorted SELECT FOR UPDATE, optimistic versions, insert-to-claim, Redis holds, an in-memory owner per event), say which isolation level each needs and where each breaks, and treat general admission as a hot counter.

Design the payment-in-flight path: a selection hold and a payment window, lazy expiry, cancel-then-release, idempotent confirmation keyed on the provider's event id, authorise-then-capture, the late-payment path and reconciliation.

Implement the waiting room (labs/c8/waitroom): idempotent FIFO joins with position and ETA, token-bucket admission capped at a burst, HMAC-signed passes verified in constant time, expiry and a bounded queue, passing under -race.

Handle the hot event past the room: rows every transaction touches, a CDN-served availability snapshot, position by sequence number and watermark, an adaptive admission rate and an honest sold-out message.
Evaluate bot and fairness controls (randomised pre-queue, registration lotteries, account and card limits, passes bound to accounts, rate limits at join) and what each costs.
